comparison: Both evaluate the same claims (C17-C29, C31-C32) about time-dependent shifts in sodium channel composition and equivalent excitability. OpenEval finds the evidence SUPPORTED with converging statistical evidence. Peer review is UNCERTAIN due to Reviewer 3's concerns about biased interpretation of 'equivalent excitability' and insufficient analysis parameters, though Reviewers 1-2 and the editor accept the findings.

Both evaluate identical claims (C34-C45) about NaV1.8's role at DIV0 using pharmacology and modeling. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the strength of dual inhibitor approach and computational validation. Peer reviewers explicitly praise the degeneracy demonstration and experimental support, with the editor confirming the data is convincing.

Both evaluate identical claims (C46-C61) about NaV1.7 and NaV1.3 necessity and interchangeability at DIV4-7. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the comprehensive pharmacological and computational evidence for degeneracy. Peer reviewers accept the functional overlap demonstration, with Reviewer 2 noting manuscript improvements during revision.

Both evaluate identical claims (C62-C67) about functional interchangeability via dynamic clamp and modeling. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the compelling nature of real-time manipulation with 100% success rates. Peer reviewers praise the elegant electrophysiology and note that computational model concerns were fixed during revision.

Both evaluate identical claims (C68-C76) about computational model predictions and experimental validation of voltage threshold differences. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the sophisticated model-experiment integration and unexpected predictions confirmed experimentally. Peer reviewers accept findings and note computational model concerns from initial review were addressed with code deposition.

Both evaluate identical claims (C77-C82) about mRNA-protein-function relationships and translation inhibition experiments. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate caution about multiple contributing mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept findings and note that protein characterization concerns from initial review were appropriately addressed in revised text.

Both evaluate identical claims (C84-C88, C99) about inflammation-induced shifts in NaV dependence in vivo. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate statistical methods and acknowledgment of increased variability. Peer reviewers accept findings as supporting main conclusions with broad scientific interest and clinical importance.

Both evaluate identical claims (C89-C91, C100) about behavioral evidence linking cellular mechanisms to altered drug efficacy. Both find the evidence SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the critical link between cellular and behavioral outcomes. Peer reviewers strongly support findings as key to clinical significance, though Reviewer 3 raises semantic objection to terminology rather than data.

Both evaluate overlapping claims about degeneracy conclusions (C95-C98, C101). OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with strong multi-method evidence (includes C115). Peer review is UNCERTAIN: Reviewers 1-2 strongly support conclusions and overall aims, but Reviewer 3 raises fundamental concerns about biased interpretation and whether equivalent excitability was properly demonstrated given different gating properties of channels.

OpenEval R10 evaluates background claims C1-C3 about clinical context. Peer R10 evaluates extensive background claims (C1-C16, C30, C33, C83, C92-C94, C102-C115). Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes appropriate citations for clinical problem motivation. Peer reviewers accept background framing and note authors appropriately discuss clinical implications without unproven speculation.

OpenEval R11 evaluates background claims C4-C11 about NaV1.7 and pain literature. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims establish complex/contradictory literature motivating the study. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context without direct critique.

OpenEval R12 evaluates background claims C12-C15 about clinical trial failures and compensation. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims motivate investigation of compensation mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context.

OpenEval R13 evaluates claims C16, C30, C33 providing background and forward references to behavioral data. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes C33 is supported by behavioral data in C89-C91. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context.

OpenEval R14 evaluates background claims C83, C92-C94 about NaV1.7, inflammation, and pain. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims provide context for inflammation findings. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context.

OpenEval R15 evaluates background claims C102-C110 about degeneracy theory and literature. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes claims establish conceptual framework for interpreting findings. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context.

OpenEval R16 evaluates claims C111-C114 integrating prior NaV gating literature with current findings. Peer R10 includes these among broader background evaluation. Both find SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes consistency with Blair and Bean (2002) validates findings. Peer reviewers accept as appropriate context.
